recentItems.title: Chingy Thinks The Government Killed 2Pac & People Around Him (Part 2)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join

Part 1: https://youtu.be/tDpGD3Z34Sc
---------

Chingy sits down with Vlad for a tense discussion about the 1996 Las Vegas shooting of 2Pac, revisiting the Death Row Records fallout, Suge Knight’s circle, and the long-debated role of Orlando Anderson after the Compton Foot Locker incident involving Travon Lane. Drawing from his own past around Bloods, Chingy challenges the common gang-retaliation narrative and shares why he believes Tupac was set up by forces beyond street beef, pointing to “dirty cops,” government involvement, and the deaths of people close to Pac.

The conversation also covers Biggie Smalls, the East Coast-West Coast feud, Outlawz member Yaki Kadafi’s death in New Jersey, bodyguards Frank Alexander and Michael Moore, Nevada security concerns, and the ongoing Keefe D murder case. Vlad pushes back with documented accounts while Chingy explains why key details still don’t add up to him.

Moe Gangat: If Lil Durk Doesn't Take the Stand He'll Get Life in Prison (Part 3)
recentItems.description:

Part 2: https://youtu.be/gKxpTYUm_vc
Part 1: https://youtu.be/fjE20W3ouPQ
--------
Attorney Moe Gangat joins Vlad to break down the high-stakes federal case involving Lil Durk, where prosecutors are relying on cooperating witnesses, alleged conspiracy evidence, and Durk’s own music, lyrics, videos, and public comments to shape the narrative for jurors. Gangat explains why testimony from Vonnie, Jam, and Flaca could be powerful despite their incentives to cooperate, and why the defense may need more than reasonable doubt to counter the government’s case.

The discussion also covers the alleged roles of Didi, Brown Eyes (David Lindsay/Keith Jones), and Boogie, whose severed trial raises questions about the wider indictment. With Durk reportedly facing life without parole, Gangat argues that if the evidence points toward conviction, taking the stand may be the only move left—even if it opens the door to tough cross-examination. A detailed legal analysis of hip-hop, federal conspiracy charges, and courtroom strategy.

--------
Charleston White sits down with Vlad for a fast-moving “This or That” centered on infamous cooperators, courtroom witnesses and street legends. White weighs Alpo Martinez against Frank Lucas, Troy Ave, Boston Richey and Finesse2Tymes before shifting to Terrance “Gangsta” Williams and his prison history. The conversation also touches trending legal headlines, including Kid Cudi and Cassie’s testimony connected to the Diddy case, plus Daphne Joy and T.I. White then breaks down Lil Woody’s unforgettable role on the stand in the YSL trial involving Young Thug, Brian Steel, Gunna and Gucci Mane, debating how the streets reacted to alleged cooperation. The round closes with Sammy “The Bull” Gravano versus Tekashi 6ix9ine, aka Daniel Hernandez, with Vlad noting 6ix9ine’s testimony and Tattletale era. Watch Charleston’s candid picks, Vlad’s pushback, and a sharp debate about loyalty, testimony and public image.

recentItems.title: Judge Mathis: Durk’s Lawyers Blaming OTF Vonnie Doesn’t Make Durk a Snitch (Part 5)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join

Part 4: https://youtu.be/Y21Rt-eE3pc
Part 1: https://youtu.be/lOCPGaKuQxw
--------
Judge Mathis sits down with Vlad to break down the legal strategy in Lil Durk’s murder case, explaining why he would vote “not guilty” based on the evidence discussed so far unless prosecutors have direct proof such as texts or audio. The longtime judge analyzes reasonable doubt, possible lesser charges, and how a jury may view claims involving OTF Vonnie. He also weighs in on the online debate over whether Durk’s defense team pointing to Vonnie as the alleged mastermind should be considered “snitching,” making clear that a lawyer’s courtroom theory is not the same as a defendant taking the stand, signing a 5K1, or making a proffer agreement. Vlad and Mathis also discuss street code, criminal cooperation, and the difference between “telling” and “snitching,” while referencing how high-profile evidence can shape public opinion in cases like Diddy and Cassie.

--------

DJ Vlad sits down with Grammy-winning producer Hit-Boy for a candid conversation about money, investing, and long-term wealth in hip-hop. Vlad explains how early stock market moves—starting with Google in 2011 and later investing in major companies like Amazon, Tesla and Apple—became central to his financial strategy beyond VladTV. Hit-Boy opens up about investing in himself, his studio setup, family, artists, and moving from a difficult deal to working with JP Morgan, money markets, the S&P 500 and NASDAQ.

The discussion also covers wealth managers, Warren Buffett, Benjamin Graham, real estate vs. stocks, prenups, divorce protection, and why Vlad says financial discipline mattered more than luxury spending. Vlad also recalls sharing stock advice with artists like Little Bibby, Mozzy and Boosie, while referencing Juice WRLD, Jay-Z, Forbes-level investing and the challenge of helping family without being taken advantage of.

Lul Tim on Getting Call Lul Pab Killed in LA, Quando Leaving Rollin 60s Crips After That (Flashback)
recentItems.description: In this flashback, Lul Tim discussed the tragic events surrounding the death of Lul Pab, who was with Quando Rondo when assailants opened fire at a gas station near the Beverly Center. Lul Tim recalled the sorrow he felt after receiving the news while under house arrest, expressing disbelief and anguish over the loss. In his interview with DJ Vlad, Quando Rondo reflected on holding Lul Pab as he died and expressed regret over his ties to the Rollin' 60s Crips, eventually renouncing his affiliation. Lul Tim also shared insight into Quando's decision to step away, acknowledging the challenges he faced and realizing that some of those associated with the group were not supportive.
